heroHeadline: Day 584: Sheinbaum Defends 53 Consulates vs. Trump Review; Inaugurates Seri Aqueduct in Sonora; INEGI April CPI 4.45% (First Deceleration of 2026); PRI Petitions Morena FTO Designation
heroSubtitle: On May 8, 2026, President Sheinbaum held a shortened mañanera before departing for a three-day Sonora working tour. She directly addressed the Trump administration's review of all 53 Mexican consulates in the U.S. — a coercive tactic previously applied to China and Russia — stating 'los consulados no realizan algún tipo de política en Estados Unidos en contra del gobierno' and defending their citizen-service mission. On the sovereignty front, she reiterated that cooperation with the U.S. is possible but subordination is not: 'it's a matter of dignity.' In Sonora, Sheinbaum inaugurated the Seri Aqueduct at Punta Chueca as the first event of her Indigenous Peoples' Justice Plan tour, with Yaqui people events, land restitution, and water infrastructure in Navojoa and Obregón to follow on May 9–10. INEGI's full April 2026 CPI release (May 7) showed annual inflation slowing to 4.45% — the first deceleration of 2026, driven by electricity subsidies and lower green vegetable prices, partially offset by rising peppers and tomatoes. PRI President Alejandro Moreno petitioned the U.S. State Department to designate Morena as a Foreign Terrorist Organization — condemned by the administration as an act of 'treason.' The first formal USMCA bilateral negotiating round remains on track for the week of May 25 in Mexico City; the market unanimously expects Banxico to cut 25bp to 6.50% at the May 14 meeting.
